summary: Standardized custom RFID cards for vibe-coding projects: a tray-printing ID card app, a 3D-printable RFID reader enclosure, and the Wish It Better framework.
origin: Not a git fork (GitHub reports fork=false), and not original either. The enclosure is the published tip of a pre-git parametric-model line in a local fab-lab workspace that predates this repo by about ten weeks: hardware/rfid-reader-case/gen_rfid_reader_case_v7.py records in its own header that it carries the tongue-and-groove-plus-bead seal and the mid-plane clamshell split from kunai_360_onex_v4.py -- the model line later published as KUNAI-001 on this same registry -- and adopts pearl_box_v2_voxel_v4.py's gyroid cell clamp verbatim -- "Orin drawer" is v7's own name for that upstream, which never uses the phrase (grep -c -i orin returns 12 in v7 and 0 in the file it names). So the two hardware projects listed here are siblings out of one Pearl Box voxel/gyroid fab method that has never been published and is on no wish-it-better manifest. This sentence read "appears in no repo" for four commits and that was false -- one of the two files named above is tracked in a private repository, which is deliberately not named here, because naming it would publish a private thing in order to correct a public sentence. src/web/vendor/qr.js states at line 22 that its structure and tables derive from Project Nayuki's QR Code generator (MIT). The Wish It Better spec this project defines was copied into the nested-resonance-memory-archive repo, making two other listed entries downstream of this one. Fragment-Mono and Instrument Serif (SIL OFL 1.1, see OFL.txt) are embedded in src/site/gt/.
amended: v1.0.1 — §1/§4: the account-free route is the minimum, not the issue tracker
_note: Level is L1. wish_channel is the wishing well on the landing page, not a mailto: a mailto is account-free but it is not a queue — it has no status, no ordering, and it made a human's inbox the precondition for anything happening. The well needs no account, no mail client and no address, and it lands in a queue an agent works. verify_pages_artifact.mjs proves the declared page actually carries the well rather than trusting the URL. `amended` carries one entry and briefly carried two: the second read "v1.0.2 — origin filled", and `git log -S` puts it in 7f0cb71, a commit that does not touch WISH_IT_BETTER.md at all. The standard records exactly one amendment in force, v1.0.1, so v1.0.2 named a spec change that never happened. §5 defines an amendment as a PR touching WISH_IT_BETTER.md AND adding the project to `amended`; filling a field in this manifest is neither half. It is deleted rather than backfilled with a genuine v1.0.2, because §5's own third rule is to write the deletion first. The reason this is not a changelog tidy: `amended` is the field L2 reads as proof of contributing back, and §5 says even v1.0.1 "earns nobody L2" because the origin project found it — so an entry with no spec change behind it is level inflation on the one file every adopter copies.
